--- title: "Visualising categorical data" subtitle: "Introduction to Global Health Data Science" date: "2026-08-26" format: revealjs: auto-stretch: false --- ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: # Recap --- ## Variables - **Numerical** variables can be classified as **continuous** or **discrete** based on whether or not the variable can take on an infinite number of values. - If the variable is **categorical**, we can determine if it is **ordinal** based on whether or not the levels have a natural ordering. --- ### Data We consider data from the Global Adult Tobacco Survey (GATS), which is designed to provide nationally-representative data on non-institutionalized people 15 years and older. This survey is a global standard for systematically monitoring adult tobacco use and is produced by the Centers for Disease Control (CDC) in collaboration with the World Health Organization (WHO), RTI International, and Johns Hopkins University. China has the largest smoking population in the world and accounts for roughly 40% of tobacco consumption worldwide. We will focus on GATS data from China in 2018 (the most recent survey year), but note data from other countries are available from the [WHO's Microdata Repository](https://extranet.who.int/ncdsmicrodata/index.php/home). --- ### Data ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} glimpse(gats) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Rows: 19,376 Columns: 18 $ CASEID 601010, 601012, 601013, 601014, 601015, … $ RESIDENCE Urban, Urban, Urban, Urban, Urban, Urban… $ PROVINCE Beijing, Beijing, Beijing, Beijing, Beij… $ REGION6 North, North, North, North, North, North… $ REGION3 East, East, East, East, East, East, East… $ AGE 33.95342, 35.92877, 70.52055, 56.95342, … $ GENDER Female, Male, Male, Male, Female, Female… $ CURRENTSMOKE No, No, No, No, Yes, No, No, No, No, Yes… $ EDUCATION High School, Postgraduate, Secondary Sch… $ OCCUPATION Other, Other, Retired, Other, Retired, B… $ AGESTART NA, NA, NA, NA, 20, NA, NA, NA, NA, 14, … $ CIGS_DAY NA, NA, NA, NA, 10, NA, NA, NA, NA, 5, N… $ HEARDOFECIG No, Yes, Yes, Yes, Yes, Yes, Yes, No, Ye… $ ECIGUSE NA, Not at All, Not at All, Not at All, … $ TRYSTOP NA, NA, NA, NA, Yes, NA, NA, NA, NA, No,… $ HOMESMOKERULES Never Allowed, Never Allowed, Never Allo… $ SMOKESICK Yes, Yes, Yes, Yes, Yes, Yes, Yes, Yes, … $ SMOKECANCER Yes, Yes, Yes, Yes, Yes, Yes, Yes, Yes, … ``` ::: ::: --- ### Selected variables | Variable | Description | |----------|-------------| | `CURRENTSMOKE` | Current smoking status (yes, no, or don't know) | | `AGE` | Computed from date of birth | | `EDUCATION` | Highest level of education completed | | `GENDER` | Interviewer-recorded gender (male, female, or missing/NA) | | `PROVINCE` | Province of residence | Other variables are also available in the dataset. Sample survey weights are not included but should be used to obtain nationally representative estimates (our unweighted estimates are fairly close for the quantities we consider today). --- # Bar plot --- ## Bar plot :::: columns ::: {.column width="60%"}
::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot(gats, aes(x = CURRENTSMOKE)) + geom_bar() ``` :::
::: ::: {.column width="40%"} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w01-04-vizcat_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-4-1.png){fig-align='center' width=100%} ::: ::: ::: :::: --- ## Stacked bar plot :::: columns ::: {.column width="60%"}
::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot( gats, aes( x = CURRENTSMOKE, fill = GENDER ) ) + geom_bar() ``` :::
::: ::: {.column width="40%"} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w01-04-vizcat_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-6-1.png){fig-align='center' width=100%} ::: ::: ::: :::: --- ## Ok, I dislike those colors :::: columns ::: {.column width="40%"}
::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot( gats, aes( x = CURRENTSMOKE, fill = GENDER ) ) + geom_bar() + scale_fill_manual( values = c( "Male" = "#012169", "Female" = "#C7BDD9" ) ) + labs( x = "Current smoker", y = "Count", fill = "Gender" ) ``` :::
::: ::: {.column width="60%"} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w01-04-vizcat_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-8-1.png){fig-align='center' width=100%} ::: ::: ::: :::: --- ## Segmented bar plot :::: columns ::: {.column width="40%"}
::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot( gats, aes( x = CURRENTSMOKE, fill = GENDER ) ) + geom_bar(position = "fill") + scale_fill_manual( values = c( "Male" = "#012169", "Female" = "#C7BDD9" ) ) + labs( x = "Current smoker", y = "Proportion", fill = "Gender" ) ``` :::
::: ::: {.column width="60%"} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w01-04-vizcat_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-10-1.png){fig-align='center' width=100%} ::: :::
Here, instead of looking at raw counts, we're looking at the proportion of smokers in each gender category.
::: :::: --- ## Which plot is more useful? :::: columns ::: {.column width="50%"} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w01-04-vizcat_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-11-1.png){fig-align='center' width=100%} ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w01-04-vizcat_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-12-1.png){fig-align='center' width=100%} ::: ::: ::: :::: --- ## Customizing bar plots :::: columns ::: {.column width="40%"}
::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot( gats, aes( y = CURRENTSMOKE, fill = GENDER ) ) + geom_bar(position = "fill") + scale_fill_manual( values = c( "Male" = "#012169", "Female" = "#C7BDD9" ) ) + labs( x = "Proportion", y = "Current Smoker?", fill = "Gender", title = "Smoking by Gender", subtitle = "2018" ) ``` :::
::: ::: {.column width="60%"} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w01-04-vizcat_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-14-1.png){fig-align='center' width=100%} ::: ::: ::: :::: --- ## Side-by-side bar plot :::: columns ::: {.column width="40%"}
::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot( gats, aes( x = CURRENTSMOKE, fill = GENDER ) ) + geom_bar(position = position_dodge()) + scale_fill_manual( values = c( "Male" = "#012169", "Female" = "#C7BDD9" ) ) + labs( x = "Current smoker", y = "Count", fill = "Gender" ) ``` :::
::: ::: {.column width="60%"} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w01-04-vizcat_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-16-1.png){fig-align='center' width=100%} ::: ::: ::: :::: --- # Relationships between numerical and categorical variables --- ## Already talked about... - Coloring and faceting histograms and density plots - Side-by-side box plots --- ## Violin plots Violin plots are like boxplots, but instead of showing the quartiles (25th, 50th, and 75th %iles), they show rotated density plots on each side. --- ## Violin plots :::: columns ::: {.column width="40%"}
::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot( gats, aes( x = AGE, y = EDUCATION ) ) + geom_violin() ``` :::
::: ::: {.column width="60%"} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w01-04-vizcat_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-18-1.png){fig-align='center' width=100%} ::: ::: ::: :::: --- ## Ridge plots Ridge plots also show density estimates across categorical groups --- ## Ridge plots :::: columns ::: {.column width="40%"}
::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} library(ggridges) ggplot( gats, aes( x = AGE, y = EDUCATION, fill = EDUCATION, color = EDUCATION ) ) + geom_density_ridges(alpha = 0.5) ``` :::
::: ::: {.column width="60%"} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w01-04-vizcat_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-20-1.png){fig-align='center' width=100%} ::: ::: ::: :::: --- ## Muted color palette :::: columns ::: {.column width="40%"}
::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} library(ggridges) duke_palette <- c( "#012169", # Duke blue "#C7BDD9", # soft lavender "#9BB7A5", # muted sage "#D6C3A5", # warm sand "#A8B7C9", # dusty blue "#C9A7A1", # dusty rose "#B9C3A3", # olive sage "#8FA4B8", # slate blue "#D9D6CC", # warm gray "#B7AFC8" # gray lavender ) ggplot( gats, aes( x = AGE, y = EDUCATION, fill = EDUCATION, color = EDUCATION ) ) + geom_density_ridges(alpha = 0.8) + scale_fill_manual(values = duke_palette) + scale_color_manual(values = duke_palette) ``` :::
::: ::: {.column width="60%"} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w01-04-vizcat_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-22-1.png){fig-align='center' width=100%} ::: ::: ::: :::: --- ## Don't need the legend :::: columns ::: {.column width="40%"}
::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} library(ggridges) duke_palette <- c( "#012169", "#C7BDD9", "#9BB7A5", "#D6C3A5", "#A8B7C9", "#C9A7A1", "#B9C3A3", "#8FA4B8", "#D9D6CC", "#B7AFC8" ) ggplot( gats, aes( x = AGE, y = EDUCATION, fill = EDUCATION, color = EDUCATION ) ) + geom_density_ridges(alpha = 0.6) + scale_fill_manual(values = duke_palette) + scale_color_manual(values = duke_palette) + theme( legend.position = "none" ) ``` :::
::: ::: {.column width="60%"} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w01-04-vizcat_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-24-1.png){fig-align='center' width=100%} ::: ::: ::: ::::

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
